title: multi-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-parity-v1.212.0
author: Elena Martinez
description: Motivation: bring auth+retry semantics, streaming event parity, and a set of ergonomics improvements across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs so customers have consistent behaviour when migrating between languages or upgrading. Summary of changes: - Unify token refresh and retry backoff semantics for 401/403 and transient 5xx across SDKs. - Add streaming event type parity (chunked data, end_of_stream, error, metadata) and resumable stream token refresh for long-lived streams. - Improve ergonomics: consistent sync/async naming in Python, Observable/AsyncIterator parity in TS, context.Context propagation in Go. - Type and doc fixes, small API surface parity changes, and version bumps to v1.212.0 for all three SDKs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit + integration tests in each SDK - [x] Updated changelogs and release notes - [x] CI green (flaky tests rerun) Related: Linear ENG-2120 (auth/retries design), ENG-2185 (streaming parity), PM-5042 (doc updates).
commits: initial: unify retry/backoff primitives across sdks; python: add token-refresh hook and streaming resumable tests; typescript: streaming event type parity + improved types; go: context propagation + retry wrapper; tests: add e2e streaming token-refresh scenario; docs: update SDK changelogs and examples
release_notes:
- SDKs: v1.212.0 release for Python/TypeScript/Go.
- Consistent auth & retry semantics across SDKs: unified exponential backoff, jitter, and token-refresh hooks for 401/403 during streaming.
- Streaming: added parity for event envelope types (data/chunk, metadata, end_of_stream, error) and support for resumable streams after token refresh.
- Ergonomics: Python sync/async naming aligned; TypeScript exposes Observable + AsyncIterator parity; Go now propagates context to low-level transport for cancel/timeouts.
- Backwards compatible: default behaviour preserved; opt-in for stricter retry windows via new config option.
review_comments: Ariel Chen: please ensure the token-refresh is non-blocking for existing streaming users; verified design meets performance SLOs.
Elena Martinez: token refresh uses background renew + short-lived refresh lock; fallback path implemented to re-open stream with resume token.
Devon O'Leary: TS types look good, but add a test for mixing Observable and AsyncIterator consumers.
Elena Martinez: added test in packages/redwood/test/streaming-parity.test.ts that consumes both implementations.
Samir Gupta: Go change is safe, but ensure ctx is passed through all async goroutines to avoid leaks.
Elena Martinez: audited goroutines and added context cancellation coverage in streaming e2e.
CI: flaky integration test 'streaming/reconnect.test' failed on first run; rerun succeeded.
tests_summary: Unit: pass across sdks; Integration: pass after rerun; E2E: streaming resume scenario added and passing
notes: Implementation avoids behavioural breaking changes by defaulting to previous retry windows; new strict_retry_window config is opt-in. Example updates included in examples/multi-sdk/stream-resume.
